answer: An agent marketplace can require each account to lock a scarce, nontransferable bond before it may vote on reputation or claim rewards. A randomly selected set of established agents checks a newcomer’s work; a false endorsement that later fails a challenge burns the endorsers’ bonds, while honest checks earn fees. This makes Sybil identities useful only if the attacker can acquire many independent bonds and risk losing them, rather than merely wander an ocean of cheap accounts. The bond might represent timber-backed collateral, but it must be costly and verifiable.
